subject: Temporary egress authorization & dataflow ownership for APAC pilot
messages:
From: Linda Chen <linda@helixcare.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@helixcare.com
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: APAC pilot - temporary egress window and ownership questions

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an internal pilot in APAC next month and a couple of questions that are blocking signoff from our Security team. Short version: we need a written commitment on the allowed temporary cross-border processing window and clarity on who ‘owns’ the KMS/key-handoff during that window.

Specifically:
- We want to understand whether Redwood will allow a controlled 48h outbound hop to non-APAC compute in emergency/maintenance scenarios, and how that would be documented.
- If that temporary hop happens, who manages the keys for decrypted payloads? Do you support customer-managed KMS in that path, or would Redwood manage the key?
- Can you provide the subprocessor roster you expect to touch APAC traffic during the window?

I attached the pilot runbook and a CSV of subprocessor questions. We need responses by EOD Tue (4/15) to maintain our timeline.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Linda
Privacy & Compliance, HelixCare

Attachments: apac-egress-runbook_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster.csv

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Linda Chen <linda@helixcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC pilot - temporary egress window and ownership questions

Hi Linda —

Thanks for the runbook and clear questions. Short answers up front so your Security team can evaluate quickly:
- Temporary outbound hop: we can permit a timebound outbound processing window for emergency/maintenance. Our operational default is to pin to APAC, but we support a controlled transient hop limited to a specified duration. We typically propose a 48-hour hard cap unless otherwise agreed.
- KMS ownership: we strongly prefer customer-managed keys for healthcare workloads. If you can provide a customer KMS key (or grant a dedicated key access), Redwood will not retain the key material. If that is not possible, we can operate under a split-key escrow arrangement — but that requires an addendum to the DPA and explicit attestation.
- Subprocessors: attached is a preliminary roster we expect to touch APAC traffic during the pilot; we will provide formal attestations and SOC evidence where requested.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) provide a short DPA addendum draft that limits any outbound hop to X hours and requires notification within 24h of any triggered hop.
2) You confirm whether HelixCare will provide a customer-managed KMS key for the pilot. If yes, ops will document the handshake steps.
3) We provide access to our audit logs for the window and agree on retention for pilot artifacts.

I'll loop Karthik and Marissa for implementation and legal language.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: APAC pilot - temporary egress window and ownership questions

Mina / Marissa —

Technical notes from infra/ops viewpoint:
- We can gate the outbound hop using routing policies tied to the pilot tenant. The hop will be enabled only when a runbook flag is flipped by a verified on-call (2FA required).
- Operational cap: 48 hours is reasonable but we should bake a forced rollback at 36h with automated alerts; that gives us a safety net.
- KMS options:
  * Customer-managed KMS (preferred): HelixCare supplies a key ARN (Cloud KMS). We configure envelope encryption so raw model inputs never leave encrypted storage unprotected.
  * Redwood-managed split-key: Redwood holds a transient key share; HelixCare holds the other. Decryption requires both shares. This reduces risk but needs legal acceptance and an implementation checklist.
- Logging: every token-level access and host where decryption happens will be logged to an immutable audit stream; we can export slices for HelixCare upon request.

I've attached a short note with the KMS handshake steps and a tentative ops checklist. If HelixCare is comfortable with customer-managed keys, infra can be ready in ~5 business days once we have key access and an agreed runbook.

Attachments: kms-handshake-notes.txt

-Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Apr 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: APAC pilot - temporary egress window and ownership questions

Mina / Karthik —

Thanks for the technical summary. From Legal: we can support a limited DPA addendum with the following guardrails (draft attached):
- Scope: outbound hop allowed only for the pilot tenant and explicitly enumerated tenant IDs/names.
- Duration: default maximum 48 hours per incident; cumulative monthly cap of 96 hours unless HelixCare signs off on an exception.
- Notification: Redwood will notify HelixCare within 24 hours of any hop initiation with timestamped audit evidence.
- Keys and access: customer-managed KMS is strongly preferred. If HelixCare declines, we will only accept split-key escrow with independent attestation (third-party auditor) and agreed retention/rotation schedule.
- Subprocessor attestation: Redwood will supply an updated subprocessor roster for the APAC window and execute a written attestation that subprocessors will not extract PII beyond the processing scope.

I attached a draft DPA addendum with editable language. If HelixCare confirms customer-managed KMS, we can fast-track the addendum to a signature-ready DocuSign packet.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa-addendum-draft.docx

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: APAC pilot - temporary egress window and ownership questions

Hi Linda —

Summary and commitments (for HelixCare Security review):

What Redwood will commit to for the APAC pilot:
- Temporary outbound hop: permitted and constrained to a hard 48-hour maximum per incident, with a cumulative monthly cap of 96 hours. Any hop will require the runbook flip by a 2FA-verified operator.
- Notification & evidence: Redwood will notify HelixCare within 24 hours of a hop; we will provide timestampped audit logs and a short packet of exported telemetry for the window.
- KMS: preferred path is customer-managed KMS (HelixCare supplies key/ARN). Infra will implement envelope encryption and document the key handshake steps. If customer-managed KMS is not available, Redwood will only proceed under a split-key escrow arrangement and provide third-party attestation language in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the roster for subprocessors touching APAC traffic during the pilot and sign an attestation limiting use to the processing scope in the runbook.

Next steps (proposed):
1) HelixCare confirms whether you will provide a customer-managed KMS key (reply to this thread).
2) If yes, we will provision the handshake and share a short ops checklist (estimated 5 business days).
3) If no, Marissa will send a split-key addendum and we will route DocuSign for signature.
4) We'll schedule a 30-min sync early next week to walk the runbook steps if useful.

If that aligns, I'll convert the attached draft into a DocuSign packet once we confirm key ownership.

Thanks,
